newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin Turks slam tightening of visa rules.
newsitem.headline: Berlin Turks slam tightening of visa rules.

text.p: Turkish community leaders in Berlin on Wednesday denounced Bonn's plan to require visas for foreign children, including those born in Germany to Turkish parents, as discriminatory and pledged to defeat it.

"Although they are now in their fourth or fifth generation in Germany, Turks are still treated as foreigners," Safter Cinar, spokesman of the Turkish Union in Berlin-Brandenburg told reporters. "This is gross discrimination."
Bonn had long waived visa requirements for children under 16 from Turkey, Morocco, Tunisia and former Yugoslavia to allow them to visit relatives for up to three months.
The Turkish Union estimated that 600,000 children in Germany and 50,000 youngsters in Berlin would be affected by the new policy. Germany invited Turkish citizens here as guest workers in the 1960s.

The Interior Ministry defended the new requirements, saying that policy had been abused by parents who were trying to get their children established here permanently in the hope they could follow on themselves.
Turkish community members complained that the new limits were the latest in a series of measures to prevent non-European Union citizens from living or working in Germany.

"People in our community are troubled by these recent developments: the visa restrictions, limits on the number of work permits given, the threat to cut the largest German Turkish cable station," Cinar told Reuters Television.
"People are wondering what will be next to go."
The Berlin-Brandenburg media commission recently limited the transmission range of the Turkish language station TRT-INT in the region's cable network.

Germany's Turkish population stands at 2.2 million, making it the largest foreign community. Berlin has nearly 150,000 Turkish citizens, making it the city with the largest Turkish population outside Turkey itself.
